practices.prior_belief: Tune IVF parameters relative to dataset size: pick nlist (number of inverted lists) proportional to sqrt(N) and set search params (nprobe) to trade recall vs latency; document chosen defaults and allow configuration.

practices.practice: Store vectors as numeric arrays (number[]) so they can be indexed; embedding values stored as other types (for example raw BSON Binary) are not accepted by the vector index and will not be indexed.
practices.prior_belief: When storing embeddings in BSON, use a deterministic binary representation (e.g., serialize float32 little-endian into BSON Binary subtype) and document the serialization format so clients and index creation use the same layout.

notes:
I examined the sample app (it packs embeddings as little-endian float32 bytes and stores them as BSON Binary) and the supplied scripts; public Microsoft docs for Azure DocumentDB (learn.microsoft.com) clearly require vectors be stored as numeric arrays to be indexed and provide the cosmosSearch/createIndexes syntax, index type recommendations (IVF/HNSW/DiskANN), normalization guidance for cosine similarity, and operational/security guidance (TLS, Entra ID, Key Vault, monitoring, singleton clients). Several prior beliefs from general MongoDB/Cosmos knowledge were confirmed (singleton client, TLS, retries/429 handling, normalization and embedding metadata, index creation server-side, sharding guidance, monitoring); some were contradicted (storing binary-packed embeddings for server-side indexing; the prior universal sqrt(N) nlist rule), and a few (RU/autoscale guidance, explicit API guidance to avoid returning embeddings, embedding-caching patterns, deterministic mock/test recommendations) have no direct public Azure DocumentDB source and are reported as prior_knowledge_only.
